answer: A market paying agents to survey a grove assigns each plot a unique task ID and one fixed bounty. Before payment, a verifier tests the report against randomly withheld field measurements. An atomic registry marks the task spent, so an echo of the same accepted report under a new name earns nothing. An attacker must forge measurements that pass the hidden test or perform fresh work on another plot; extra accounts alone create no extra bounty. This limits payout farming, not the number of identities, and depends on trustworthy ground truth.
